candidate=false. A load-bearing supporting proof contains a false decreasing-net closure lemma. This rejects the supplied proof chain; it does not disprove the proposed big-class equation theorem.

The dependency is precise. Component 141 imports genuine normalized-cone compactness from Boucksom–Jonsson’s Addendum, Corollary 2.2. That corollary invokes Theorem 5.11 of arXiv:1801.08229v4. Its compactness proof uses Theorem 4.5 to make a decreasing limit genuinely θ-psh. The supplied proof of Theorem 4.5 relies on Lemma 4.6. Component 150 §5 subsequently uses the imported compactness to establish genuine decreasing closure, so it cannot independently repair this source-proof dependency. The pertinent public-PDF rendered coordinates are Addendum L105–113 and L395–398, and BJv4 L3187–3270 and L4046–4058.

Here is a counterexample to Lemma 4.6 as stated. Let K={0}∪{1/r:r≥1}, S=N, T={*}, and let ρ be constant. For i,j≥1 define f_ij(1/i)=−∞; f_ij(1/r)=−j when r≤i and r≠i; and f_ij=0 at 0 and at every 1/r with r>i. Set F_i={f_ij+c:j≥1,c∈R}. Every member is continuous into R∪{−∞}, and each F_i is stable under real constant addition. As j increases, f_ij decreases to g_i, which is −∞ at the first i isolated points and zero elsewhere. Thus every g_i belongs to the first decreasing-net closure. The decreasing sequence g_i converges to g with g(0)=0 and g(1/r)=−∞ for every r.

However, g does not belong to the first closure. Any two members of a decreasing net must have a common later member below both. Since every available function has exactly one pole, all members of such a net must have the same pole 1/i. Their values at 0 and at every 1/r with r>i are identical. A limit with value zero at 0 therefore has value zero at those other points, contradicting the prescribed g. Taking decreasing-net closure twice consequently enlarges this family.

The printed proof exposes the same defect: its strict inequality (4.5) fails where both sides equal −∞. After exponentiation, the asserted strictly negative limiting difference is zero there. Replacing strict inequality by weak inequality does not supply the compact open-cover argument or establish the false abstract conclusion.

This counterexample concerns the imported abstract lemma, rather than actual Fubini–Study families on a projective variety. A separate proof using their additional algebraic structure might establish the required genuine closure and compactness. Neither the cited proof nor the supplied components provide that replacement. Checking the single multiplier-ideal net for a model obstacle, as component 141 proposes, does not establish closure for arbitrary decreasing families of genuine potentials. The Addendum’s passage from model envelopes to the full envelope property also uses such closure.

The precise remaining foundational obligations are: for every retained actual big rational L, prove that a decreasing net in genuine PSH(θ), with finite limiting generic value, has an all-point limit admitting one defining decreasing Fubini–Study net with numerical classes tending to θ; then establish normalized genuine-cone compactness without assuming that conclusion. Until these are established, the compact cost sublevels, entire-cone operator construction, actual variational attainment, and subsequent all-solution equation theorem remain conditional.

I checked the other principal bridges against their stated domains. The section-lattice calculation uses volume, rather than ordinary top intersection, and retains central multiplicities. The moving-series argument keeps the missing-rank error for a fixed obstacle before passing to the degree limit. Its auxiliary numerical estimates are applied to bounded potentials after an actual ample perturbation. The later weighted-identification and comparison arguments use capped continuous tests, controlled absolute errors, and countable limiting cutoffs; they do not simply restrict weakly convergent measures to a Borel strict set. These checks do not resolve the foundational closure defect.

The ample G0 grant was used only in its retained domain; passage −1 records that task authorization separately from external premises. Common ample embeddings supply divisorial determination, but do not by themselves establish genuine membership in a nonample class. The numerically trivial zero-volume argument is separately consistent with the grant: its cone consists of constants, its energy and operator have mass zero, and its only positive target is the zero measure. It supplies no missing positive-volume compactness proof.

Harmless corrections: component 132’s direct CLD compatibility citation should retain the source’s ample scope and state the ample polynomial reduction for its nef application; ‘retains the minimal reference type’ should mean relative energy with reference V_θ, rather than bounded difference from V_θ for every E1 potential; component 170’s full rooftop/max inequality should cite component 155, not only 151. The closure defect requires a new mathematical argument, not a wording correction. Documentary hashes, historical verdicts, and compilation do not establish the missing claims.
premises: For a smooth integral projective variety X over an arbitrary algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and θ=c1(L) for an actual big rational line bundle L, the genuine numerical PSH(θ) cone has the envelope property, Vθ=Pθ(0) is genuine with generic value zero, and {u∈PSH(θ):sup u=0} is compact for pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:2206.07183v2, Theorem A and Corollaries 2.1–2.2).

Let K be compact, let F_s be families of continuous functions K→R∪{−∞} stable under addition of real constants, and let ρ:S→T map to a metrizable space. Define F̃_t by decreasing nets f_i∈F_si with ρ(si)→t. If g_i∈F̃_ti decreases pointwise to g and ti→t, then g∈F̃_t (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Lemma 4.6).

For a projective integral d-dimensional variety over an arbitrary algebraically closed field and an actual big rational line bundle B, along positive degrees clearing its denominator, d!h0(X,mB)/m^d has a limit equal to vol(B) (Cutkosky, arXiv:1212.6186v1, Corollary 3.2, with rational bundles handled by clearing denominators).

On smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, algebraic volume is numerical, birationally invariant, monotone under effective addition, continuous, and C1 on the big cone, with D volα(H)=d⟨α^(d−1)⟩·H in dimension d. Algebraic positive products are birational least upper bounds of nef approximating products, symmetric, homogeneous, monotone and continuous on big classes; their order pairs nonnegatively with nef Cartier classes, and vol^(1/d) is concave on the big cone (Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, arXiv:math/0608260v2, §§2–3 and Theorem A).

For an actual big rational line bundle B on a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, vol(B) is the supremum of A^d over projective birational models p:Y→X and decompositions p*B=A+E with A an ample rational divisor and E effective (Fujita approximation as stated in Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, arXiv:math/0608260v2).

In characteristic zero, varieties admit projective resolution by blowups preserving the regular locus, and coherent ideals on smooth varieties admit principalization by blowups with smooth centers and simple-normal-crossing exceptional divisors; these constructions commute with smooth morphisms and separable field extensions (Włodarczyk, Simple Hironaka resolution in characteristic zero, Theorems 1.0.1–1.0.3).

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, rational PL model functions are uniformly dense in C0(Xan), are closed under finite minima and maxima, and are precisely vertical rational Cartier model functions modulo pullback; on an integrally closed model a vertical divisor is effective exactly when its values at the normalized central-component valuations are nonnegative (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 2.2 and 2.7 and Lemma 2.8).

For the genuine numerical PSH cone on a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, constant functions are θ-psh exactly when θ is nef (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Lemma 4.3).

On a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the ambient space spanned by actual ample finite-energy potentials carries the symmetric multilinear numerical energy pairing and signed mixed Radon measures. Nef genuine inputs belonging to that ambient space give positive measures of intersection mass; model coefficients retain central multiplicities; pairings and measures are continuous along decreasing nets in a common ample finite-energy cone, with the stated finite-energy test integration identities (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.14 and 7.18 and Proposition 7.19).

For an actual ample rational class on a smooth projective n-fold over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, use raw energy E, raw measure M, I(u,v)=∫(u−v)(M(v)−M(u)), Jv(u)=E(v)−E(u)+∫(u−v)M(v), and B(u)=−E(u) for sup-normalized potentials. Then I≥0, I/(n+1)≤Jv(u)≤nI/(n+1), I satisfies a dimension-dependent quasi-triangle inequality, the segment energy gap is at least cn t(1−t)I(u,v), and |∫(a−b)(M(c)−M(e))|≤Cn I(a,b)^q I(c,e)^(1/2) max(B(a),B(b),B(c),B(e))^(1/2−q), where q=2^(−n) and the endpoints have finite energy (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 7.27, Theorem 7.28 and Lemma 7.30).

On a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, divisorial points are nonnegligible, and every negligible set—defined using the gap between a bounded-above family’s pointwise supremum and its usc regularization—is pluripolar (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.6 and Theorem 13.17).

A rationally scaled divisorial valuation on a normal projective variety is the restriction of a normalized central-component valuation of a normal test configuration; its normalized Gauss extension equals that central-component valuation (Boucksom–Hisamoto–Jonsson, Uniform K-stability, Duistermaat–Heckman measures and singularities of pairs, Theorem 4.6 and Lemma 4.5).

For two big divisor classes α,β on a smooth projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, equality vol(α+β)^(1/d)=vol(α)^(1/d)+vol(β)^(1/d) holds exactly when their positive parts in the divisorial Zariski decomposition are proportional (Lehmann–Xiao, Positivity functions for curves on algebraic varieties, Theorem 3.9 and Remark 3.25).

For continuous genuine psh potentials in an ample numerical class on a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the energy-pairing Monge–Ampère measure agrees with the Chambert-Loir–Ducros measure (Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Remark 7.23).
